subject: general
question: An object is placed 30 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. What will be the image distance v ?
solution:
The correct answer is __**–30 cm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The question is about determining the **image distance (v)** when an object is placed in front of a concave mirror. The given parameters are:

 
 
• **Object distance (u) = –30 cm**. (The object distance is negative as per the sign convention because the object is placed in front of the mirror.)
 
• **Focal length (f) = –15 cm**. (The focal length of a concave mirror is negative as it lies on the same side as the object.)
 
 
 
• The mirror formula is given by: **1/f = 1/v + 1/u**
 
• Substitute the values of **f** and **u**:
 
 
• **1/–15 = 1/v + 1/–30**
 
• Simplify: **1/v = 1/–15 – 1/–30**
 
• Take the LCM of –15 and –30: **1/v = –2/30 + 1/30**
 
• Further simplify: **1/v = –1/30**
 
• So, **v = –30 cm**.
 
 
 
• The negative sign of **v** indicates that the image is formed on the same side as the object, which means the image is **real and inverted**.
 
• *Hence, the correct image distance is **–30 cm**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sign Convention for Mirrors:**

 
 
• All distances are measured from the pole of the mirror.
 
• Distances measured in the direction of the incident light (towards the mirror) are taken as **negative**.
 
• Distances measured in the direction opposite to the incident light (away from the mirror) are taken as **positive**.
 
• The focal length of a concave mirror is always **negative**, while that of a convex mirror is **positive**.
 
 
 
• **Nature of Image Formed by a Concave Mirror:**
 
 
• If the object is beyond the focal point (f), the image formed is **real, inverted, and on the same side as the object**.
 
• If the object is at the focal point, the image is formed at **infinity**.
 
• If the object is between the focal point and the pole, the image is **virtual, upright, and magnified**.
 
 
 
• **Mirror Formula:**
 
 
• The mirror formula relates the focal length (f), object distance (u), and image distance (v): **1/f = 1/v + 1/u**.
 
• It is valid for both concave and convex mirrors, provided the correct sign convention is followed.
 
 
 
• **Magnification:**
 
 
• The magnification (M) of a mirror is given by: **M = –v/u**.
 
• A positive magnification indicates an **upright image**, while a negative magnification indicates an **inverted image**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Real Image:** A real image is formed when the rays of light converge after reflection or refraction. It can be projected onto a screen.
 
• **Virtual Image:** A virtual image is formed when the rays of light appear to diverge from a point but do not actually meet. It cannot be projected onto a screen.
 
• **Applications of Concave Mirrors:**
 
 
• Used in torches and vehicle headlights to produce a strong, focused beam of light.
 
• Used by dentists for magnified and focused views of teeth.
 
• Used in solar concentrators to focus sunlight on a single point.
 
 
 
• **Convex Mirrors:** Used as rear-view mirrors in vehicles because they provide a wider field of view.
